analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers Bernoulli equation relating static, dynamic and total pressure, its macro scale derivation from energy and enthalpy under steady inviscid incompressible assumptions, molecular interpretation and applications to tube flow, airfoils and pitot tubes.

overview.headline: Bernoulli equation linking pressure and velocity in steady incompressible flow

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the constant total pressure equals static plus dynamic contributions throughout the flow.
keyPoints.quote: We call this constant the total pressure pt of the flow.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that Bernoulli form applies only to inviscid incompressible steady flow without heat addition and negligible height change.
keyPoints.quote: the restrictions for this form are that the flow is inviscid, incompressible, steady, without heat addition, and with negligible change in height.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that dynamic pressure is density times the square of the velocity divided by two.
keyPoints.quote: The form of the dynamic pressure is the density times the square of the velocity divided by two.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that static pressure plus dynamic pressure equals original total pressure when energy is conserved in the flow.
keyPoints.quote: the static pressure plus the dynamic pressure is equal to the original total pressure in a flow

keyTerms.gloss: Pressure from random motion of molecules in the flow
keyTerms.quote: The remaining random motion of the molecules still produces a pressure called the static pressure.

keyTerms.gloss: Pressure associated with ordered motion of the gas
keyTerms.quote: We call this pressure the dynamic pressure.

keyTerms.gloss: Constant sum of static and dynamic pressure throughout the flow
keyTerms.quote: We call this constant the total pressure pt of the flow.

keyTerms.gloss: Flow condition that neglects viscous dissipation of energy
keyTerms.quote: the restrictions for this form are that the flow is inviscid, incompressible, steady, without heat addition, and with negligible change in height.

keyTerms.gloss: Flow condition where density remains constant along the streamline
keyTerms.quote: the restrictions for this form are that the flow is inviscid, incompressible, steady, without heat addition, and with negligible change in height.

keyTerms.gloss: Single flow path where Bernoulli equation holds along the constant
keyTerms.quote: an assumption was also introduced that restricts this equation to be true only along a single streamline.

keyTerms.gloss: Total fluid energy measure that combines internal energy and pressure work
keyTerms.quote: where ht is the total enthalpy of the fluid, q is the heat transfer into the fluid, and Wsh is the useful work done by the fluid.
